=== CALL C0306 ===
Ryan: Here we go, can you hear me alright, mate?
Gareth: Yeah. Yeah, fine.
Ryan: Sound. I'm Ryan, I'm in Stockport. Well, I work in Manchester, but I'm kipping in Stockport, do you know what I mean.
Gareth: Gareth. Basingstoke.
Ryan: Basingstoke! Never been. I've been through it on the train, I think. Is it all roundabouts? Someone told me it's all roundabouts.
Gareth: Er, there's a few, yeah. It's sort of known for that.
Ryan: Ha, I knew it. Here, how'd you get on with that puzzle thing at the start? I was flying for the first bit, then the one with the shapes, the rotating ones, I just sat there, mate, I just stared at it. I reckon I guessed the last three.
Gareth: Er, that one was alright actually. It's kind of what I do all day.
Ryan: Go on then, what do you do?
Gareth: Structural engineer. Warehouses mostly, retail units. Working out if the steel's big enough, basically.
Ryan: That's a proper job, that. That's the one where if you get it wrong the roof comes in, isn't it?
Gareth: Pretty much, yeah.
Ryan: No pressure then. I run a bar, me, music venue in the Northern Quarter. So if I get it wrong, the worst that happens is a band turns up and there's no lager, which, to be fair, is nearly as bad. I've got about eighteen staff, I do the booking, licensing, all that. Love it, honestly, apart from the spreadsheets. The owners want everything on a spreadsheet. I'm like, mate, it's a bar, just come in on a Friday and look, it's rammed.
Gareth: Yeah. I'm not great on the admin side either.
Ryan: Are you not? See, I'd have had you down as a spreadsheet man.
Gareth: Calcs, yeah. Timesheets, no. They go in late every month.
Ryan: Ha! There you go, we'd get on. Here, what's on your fridge there, is that a Saints magnet?
Gareth: Yeah, fixtures. Southampton. My dad's lot, so I didn't really get a choice.
Ryan: Same with me and County. Stockport County, season ticket, Edgeley Park, I take my nephew. He's twelve, he's just got into it properly this year and now he knows more than me, it's doing my head in. He's correcting me on stats in the car.
Gareth: My lad's fifteen. We go to St Mary's a couple of times a season.
Ryan: That's good, that. Is he into it?
Gareth: Er, yeah, when he's not on his phone. He should be revising, GCSE year next year. He says he is.
Ryan: He's not.
Gareth: No, he's not.
Ryan: Ha! I wasn't either. I left uni after a year, so I'm not the one to ask, but you turned out alright, didn't you, with the steel and that. Do you still play at all? I do five-a-side Wednesdays and I've got into padel, have you tried padel? It's like tennis but in a cage, it's mint, honestly, I'm obsessed.
Gareth: No. I did five-a-side till my late thirties. Group sort of drifted off.
Ryan: You want to get back into it, mate. Or padel, padel's easier on the knees.
Gareth: Maybe. I walk the dog mostly. Bonnie. That's about it.
Ryan: That counts. My sister's got a dog, she walks it in the rain at six in the morning, she's a machine. I'm at her place at the minute actually, spare room, long story.
Gareth: Right. Yeah.
Ryan: Bit embarrassing at thirty-seven, but she does a cracking tea, so I'm not complaining. Do you do the cooking, or—
Gareth: Yeah, me. Spag bol, chilli. Friday's takeaway, that's the highlight, to be honest.
Ryan: Friday takeaway's sacred. What do you go for, Chinese?
Gareth: Usually, yeah. Or a Domino's if the kids win.
Ryan: Oh, you've got to come up to Manchester, mate, there's this Vietnamese place round the corner from work, I'm telling you—

=== CALL C0307 ===
Craig: Hiya, er, can you hear us alright?
Gemma: Yeah, hiya. Can you hear me?
Craig: Aye, loud and clear. I'm Craig.
Gemma: Oh. That's my husband's name. *(laughs)* Sorry, that threw me a bit. I'm Gemma.
Craig: Ha, good name, that. Where are you, then?
Gemma: Bloxwich. It's Walsall, sort of. West Midlands.
Craig: Right, aye. I'm Hartlepool, up the North East, on the coast.
Gemma: Is that near Newcastle?
Craig: Bit further down, like, between Sunderland and Middlesbrough. Everyone says Newcastle, it's fine. Yeah... er. Was that puzzle alright for you? I sort of lost the plot halfway through.
Gemma: Erm, no, I was rubbish at the shapes one. I just clicked something in the end.
Craig: Same. I thought it was just me, honestly.
Gemma: No, definitely not just you.
Craig: What do you do yourself, Gemma?
Gemma: I just run a shift really. At a parcel depot off the M6, by Cannock. Late shift.
Craig: How many on a shift, like?
Gemma: About forty. And two team leaders.
Craig: Forty! That's not "just" anything, that. That's a lot of folk to keep happy.
Gemma: *(laughs)* Erm, I don't know. Most of them are alright, to be fair. It's the run-up to Christmas you dread, it's rammed, parcels everywhere. Sorry, what do you do?
Craig: Er, I'm a brickie. Well, I was. I've been off with me back about a year and a half now, so I'm sort of in between things, you know.
Gemma: Oh, that's rubbish. Sorry.
Craig: Nah, it's alright, it's just one of them things. The physio says walk, so I walk the seafront. The wind coming in off the sea, though, it'd take your face off.
Gemma: My Craig's a plasterer. Self-employed. He's always going on about his back as well.
Craig: Aye, tell him to look after it, 'cause I didn't. You think you're fine till you're not, like. You're lifting blocks all day and you don't think twice. Then one morning I bent down to tie me boot and that was it, couldn't get back up. Me mam had to ring the doctor for us. Thirty-three and me mam's ringing the doctor.
Gemma: Oh no. That must've been horrible.
Craig: Aye, it was a bit daft really. Anyway. Does he leave dust everywhere? Plasterers are the worst for it. We used to say you could follow 'em round site by the footprints.
Gemma: *(laughs)* Yeah, it's all over the van. And the hall. I've given up. Dolly comes in white sometimes. She's our dog.
Craig: Is that her in the corner there? I can see an ear.
Gemma: Yeah, that's her. She's a Staffie, she's old now, her hips are dodgy. She just sleeps on me.
Craig: Ah, bless her. We never had a dog, me mam wouldn't have it. My daughter's always on about one, Ellie, she's nine. Every other weekend she asks.
Gemma: Aww. Is that her in the photo behind you?
Craig: Aye, that's her school photo. She hates it 'cause her fringe is wonky.
Gemma: She looks lovely.
Craig: Ta. She's a good kid. Er, yeah. What do you get up to when you're not at work, then?
Gemma: Erm, not much really. Walk Dolly. Jigsaws in winter, I've had one on the go three weeks. And a quiz down the pub with my sister.
Craig: Are you any good?
Gemma: Not really, my sister is. I do the music round. Nineties stuff, do you know what I mean.
Craig: You'd be alright with me then, I only know Oasis.
Gemma: *(laughs)* That's half the round, to be fair.
Craig: Ha, aye. Here, what's the food like at a depot? Do they feed yous?
Gemma: There's a bacon bap van outside. Best bit of the job, honestly.
Craig: A bap. Me mam calls 'em bread buns. She'd have a fit if I said bap in the house—

=== CALL C0308 ===

Aleena: No, that's a bit of a stupid thing to say, you don't even know me. I'm brilliant at it. I'm the top seller on add-ons at work. I can get anyone to buy socks.

Ryan: It's a compliment! What do you listen to, then? Go on, judge yourself.
Aleena: UK rap, Afrobeats, whatever's on TikTok. And Malayalam film songs when my mum's driving, but that's not my choice.
Ryan: We do an Afrobeat night once a month, it's rammed, it's one of the best nights we do. Whose turntable do you reckon that is behind me?
Aleena: Yours, obviously. Do you DJ, then?
Ryan: At mates' parties, yeah. I'm decent, to be fair. Better than most of the lads they book.
Aleena: Everyone says that, though.
Ryan: Not everyone's right, though, are they? I am.
Aleena: Okay, go on then, what's the last thing you—

=== CALL C0309 ===
Kerry: Hiya! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me okay?
Gareth: Yeah. Hi.
Kerry: Great. I'm Kerry, I'm down in Taunton. Somerset.
Gareth: Gareth. Basingstoke.
Kerry: Ooh, Basingstoke. I've only ever seen it from the M3, to be honest. Is that a dog lead on your cupboard there?

Kerry: Snap, look, mine's on the back door. Moss, springer spaniel, he's ten. Went up the Quantocks on Sunday and he rolled in something absolutely disgusting, had to hose him down in the garden. Darren was not impressed.

Kerry: Fox is the worst, isn't it? You can't get the smell off. So what do you do, Gareth?

Gareth: *(pause)* Yeah. Sort of, yeah.
Kerry: Sorry, that was a terrible joke. Is that what you'd call it, checking they're not broken?
Gareth: More checking they won't break. Before they're built.
Kerry: Ah, see, I only get them after. People come in having fallen off a ladder, and I'm there going, right, arm up for me, my love. It's mostly general X-ray, a bit of CT. And the car park's a nightmare, that's the main thing about my job really. Twenty minutes going round some mornings.
Gareth: Sorry, say that again? You cut out a bit.
Kerry: The car park. Nightmare. Twenty minutes.
Gareth: Ah. The A33's like that for me. Roadworks.
Kerry: Do you drive in every day?
Gareth: Three days. Home the other two. Suits me with the kids.
Kerry: How many have you got?
Gareth: Two. Fifteen and twelve. Callum and Ellie.
Kerry: Oh, lovely. Busy, then.
Gareth: Yeah. I forgot it was non-uniform day last week. Ellie went in in her uniform and everyone else was in their own clothes.
Kerry: Oh no! *(laughs)* Was she furious?
Gareth: Pretty furious, yeah. I'm on my own with them most of the week, so it's sort of on me now.
Kerry: Well, honestly, I'd forget too. That's why I have the calendar on the wall there, everything goes on it, all my shifts, Darren's jobs, the dog's jabs. And I do a spreadsheet for the camping. We go to Bude every summer with friends and I do the packing list for everyone. They take the mick, but nobody's ever forgotten a tent peg.
Gareth: I took the kids to a caravan in Devon once. I forgot the bedding.
Kerry: All the bedding?
Gareth: All of it.
Kerry: *(laughs)* Oh, Gareth. You need me. Did you at least have a cream tea while you were down there?
Gareth: Yeah, think so.
Kerry: Jam first or cream first?
Gareth: Er. Didn't really think about it.
Kerry: Well, you're in Devon, they'd have done cream first, which is wrong. Jam first, always. I'll die on that hill.
Gareth: Fair enough. I just eat it.
Kerry: That's the most dangerous answer you could've given. Sorry, am I going on? Do you get to watch much football with all that?
Gareth: Saints, yeah. On the telly mostly. I go a couple of times a—

=== CALL C0310 ===
Ryan: Alright, mate! Can you hear me?
Craig: Aye, yeah, hiya. I'm Craig.
Ryan: Ryan. Stockport. Here, is that a Pools scarf on your door?
Craig: *(laughs)* Aye, Hartlepool. Didn't think anyone'd spot that.
Ryan: Mate, I spot scarves. I've got County on the shelf here, look. Stockport County. Season ticket.
Craig: Oh, aye, I saw that on your photo. Yous were in the National League with us for a bit, weren't you?
Ryan: We were, yeah, dark times. Dark times, Craig. Do you still go?
Craig: Er, when money allows, like. I had a season ticket for years. Me and me dad used to go every home game, from when I was about six. He's passed now, so it's sort of not the same. I watch most of 'em down the pub now, or on me phone.
Ryan: Ah, sorry, mate. That's rough.
Craig: Nah, it's alright. It's a long time ago now. Still miss him at the football, mind.
Ryan: Yeah. My dad had a heart scare a couple of years back, and it properly shook me, honestly. He's fine now, he's back moaning about the ref. But you think, don't you.
Craig: Aye. You do.
Ryan: Anyway! What do you do for work, then?
Craig: Er, I'm a brickie. Well, I was. Done me back about eighteen month ago, so I'm off at the minute. Universal Credit and that. Bit embarrassing, to be honest.
Ryan: Nah, don't be daft, that's not embarrassing. Backs go. Half my five-a-side lads have got a dodgy back and they still play, which is worse. What would you do instead, like, if you couldn't go back on the bricks?
Craig: I've been sort of thinking site supervisor, maybe. Or building maintenance. Something where I'm not lifting blocks all day. There's a course through the job centre I might look at.
Ryan: You'd be good at that, you. You've got the calm face. Supervisors need the calm face. I haven't got it, my staff say I'm blunt. I am blunt, to be fair.
Craig: *(laughs)* Aye, I was always the one keeping the peace on site, like. Someone'd be kicking off about the weather and I'd just crack on.
Ryan: See? That's a skill, that. I'm a manager, I run a bar in Manchester, and half the job's just stopping people kicking off. I'd hire you tomorrow.
Craig: Ha, I'd be no good behind a bar, I'd drop everything.
Ryan: You'd be on the door, mate. Here, I'm going to be honest, I'm living in my sister's spare room at the minute. Since the divorce. Thirty-seven, in a single bed. So you're not the only one.
Craig: No way. I'm back at me mam's. Same bedroom I had when I was a kid. Divorce and all.
Ryan: Ha! Look at us. The lads' club.
Craig: Aye. It's alright, though. Me mam does me tea, half five, mince and dumplings. Can't complain.
Ryan: My sister does tea and all. Best thing about it. Do you have kids?
Craig: Me daughter, Ellie, she's nine. Every other weekend. That's her on the wall there.
Ryan: Ah, she's got a cracking smile. Does she go to the match with you?
Craig: She's been once. She spent the whole game asking for chips.
Ryan: That's the proper football experience, that. My nephew was the same, now he's correcting my stats in the car. Give it a couple of years, she'll be—

=== CALL C0311 ===
Gemma: Hiya. Erm, can you hear me?
Gareth: Yeah. Hi.
Gemma: I'm Gemma.
Gareth: Gareth.
Gemma: *(pause)* Where are you, then?
Gareth: Basingstoke.
Gemma: Oh, right. I'm Walsall. Bloxwich.
Gareth: Right.
Gemma: *(laughs)* Sorry, I'm not very good at these.
Gareth: No, me neither. That's fine.
Gemma: Have you done many?
Gareth: This is the third. The last two did most of the talking, to be honest.
Gemma: Same. Well, my first one was nice, he was easy. Erm. What do you do?
Gareth: Structural engineer. Warehouses mainly.
Gemma: Oh, I work in one. Well, a depot. Parcel sorting, off the M6. I run the late shift.
Gareth: Big shed? Steel portal frame, probably.
Gemma: I don't know, to be fair. It's big. It's got a big roof. *(laughs)*
Gareth: Yeah, that'll be it. Most of them are. I've probably done one like it. You spend weeks on the calcs and then you drive past it and it's just a big grey box.
Gemma: Does it not feel weird, though? Like, you know it's your one?
Gareth: Bit, yeah. The kids don't care. I point and they don't look up.
Gemma: How old are they?
Gareth: Fifteen and twelve.
Gemma: Is that their school shirts behind you? On the airer?
Gareth: *(laughs)* Yeah. Ironing's not happening.
Gemma: Mine's the same, I just hang stuff up and hope. Craig does most of the tea on my shift days, my husband. I do four long shifts a week, so by the end I'm knackered, I can't even think.
Gareth: Late finish?
Gemma: Gone eleven, sometimes later. And then I can't sleep straight after, so I'm sat up with Dolly. That's her, the ear in the corner.
Gareth: Ah. What is she?
Gemma: Staffie. She's twelve, her hips have gone a bit. The vet bills, honestly.
Gareth: Yeah. Bonnie's getting there. Labrador cross. She was the kids' dog really, but it's me walks her.
Gemma: That's always how it goes, isn't it.
Gareth: Pretty much, yeah. *(pause)* I'm on my own with them, mostly. Their mum's in Reading.
Gemma: Oh. That's a lot on you, though, with work as well.
Gareth: Sort of, yeah. I muddle through. Forgot non-uniform day last week.
Gemma: *(laughs)* Oh no. My mum did that to me once and I've never let her forget it.
Gareth: Ellie won't let me forget it either.
Gemma: Ellie, that's funny, the bloke I just spoke to, his daughter's called Ellie.
Gareth: Popular one. *(pause)* Do you like it, then? Running the shift?
Gemma: Erm. I like the people, most of them. I don't like the paperwork. Or when you have to let someone go, I lie awake over that. Sorry, does that answer it?
Gareth: Yeah. I'm the same with paperwork. Timesheets.
Gemma: My team leader chases mine, to be fair. I'd be lost without her.
Gareth: Probably need one of those.
Gemma: Everyone needs one of those. *(laughs)* Would you go back to the office full-time, if they—

=== CALL C0312 ===
Craig: Hiya, er, can you hear us?
Gareth: Yeah. Hi. Gareth.
Craig: Craig. Hartlepool.
Gareth: Basingstoke.
Craig: Right, aye. *(pause)* Yeah... er. Is that your fourth one?
Gareth: Yeah. Last one, I think.
Craig: Same. I'm getting the hang of it now, like. First one I was sat here sweating.
Gareth: *(laughs)* Yeah. Bit odd, talking to a screen.

Craig: Do you go much?
Gareth: Couple of times a season. With my lad, Callum. He's fifteen.
Craig: Ah, that's nice, that. I used to go with me dad every home game. He's gone now, so. You want to keep doing that with him, you know.

Craig: Ah, sorry, mate. It's hard when you've got kids and work and that.
Gareth: Yeah. No excuse really.
Craig: Nah, you're doing your best, like. Er, have you got a daughter as well, then? Only, Gemma said, I think, someone had an Ellie.
Gareth: Yeah, Ellie. Twelve.
Craig: No way! Mine's Ellie and all. Nine. That's her on the wall.
Gareth: *(laughs)* Gemma said that to me, yeah. Popular name.

Gareth: Doesn't sound daft. *(pause)* We're about eighteen months in. Not divorced, just separated. Nobody's done the paperwork.
Craig: Ah, right. Paperwork's the worst bit, honestly. Did me head in.
Gareth: Yeah. I'm bad at paperwork anyway. Probably why it's not done.
Craig: *(laughs)* Fair enough. What do you do, then?
Gareth: Structural engineer. Warehouses, retail units.
Craig: Oh, aye? I'm a brickie. Well, was. Done me back. So I've probably built the walls you've drawn, like.
Gareth: *(laughs)* Probably, yeah. Blockwork infill on a portal frame, that's half my drawings.
Craig: That's half me working life, that. Laying blocks in the rain off some drawing an engineer did in a warm office.
Gareth: Sorry about that.
Craig: Nah, you're alright. I'm thinking of going for site supervisor, maybe. If me back holds up.
Gareth: You'd get on alright. Good supervisors are hard to find. Most of the ones I deal with just shout.
Craig: Aye, I'm not a shouter. Is it—

=== CALL C0313 ===
Kerry: Hiya! There we go. Can you hear me?
Ryan: Loud and clear. Ryan, Stockport. You're Kerry, yeah? I said in the photo bit you look exactly like my sister. The calendar, the kettle, all of it.

Kerry: See, that's my nightmare. Is that what you're after, someone to tell you you're brave?
Ryan: *(laughs)* Bit, yeah. Bit—

=== CALL C0314 ===

Gemma: *(laughs)* Hiya. Yeah, that's Dolly. She won't get off me.
Aleena: I'm Aleena, I'm in Swansea. Not Cardiff.
Gemma: Gemma. Walsall. Erm, I wouldn't have said Cardiff.
Aleena: Everyone does, it's my thing now. Have you had Ryan yet? The Manchester one?
Gemma: No. I've had... Craig, and Gareth.
Aleena: Oh my god, he's so loud. He's nice, though. He told me recruitment was soul-destroying and I was like, you don't even know me. *(laughs)* So what do you do?
Gemma: I run a shift. At a parcel depot. Off the M6.
Aleena: Wait, parcels? Like Evri and stuff?
Gemma: Sort of, yeah. Couriers, that kind of thing.
Aleena: Stop. I sell on Vinted. I'm probably sending you stuff every week. Do you see the parcels, like, actually?

Aleena: Trainers, mostly. Clothes. I sold some Air Forces last week for double what I paid.
